sh: Board of Peace warns Gaza truce at risk
headline: Trump’s Board of Peace warns the Gaza ceasefire could collapse and faults Israel and Hamas
summary: The US-led Board of Peace, which oversees the Gaza ceasefire, told the UN Security Council that the truce is in danger of collapse. Its report, made public on 18 November, says both Israel and Hamas have failed to meet their commitments.
why: The ceasefire has held for about 13 months, but the war has not formally ended and most people in Gaza still live in ruins or tents. If the truce collapses, full-scale fighting could resume.

event.t: The board’s report to the UN Security Council says Israel and Hamas have both fallen short of their commitments under the 2025 ceasefire deal, leaving people in Gaza in dire conditions.

It warns that the gap between what was agreed and what is happening on the ground is the main risk to the truce, citing continued military activity, limits on aid and delays in setting up a civilian administration.
The board says Palestinians face another winter in tents and rubble, and urges the Security Council to support the deal.
Senior Hamas official Basem Naim called the report disinformation and accused the board of covering for Israel.

effects.label: People in Gaza
effects.t: Winter in tents, with aid still limited.

effects.label: Ceasefire
effects.t: The board says the truce cannot last if nothing changes on the ground.

watch: The Security Council meeting on the report at the end of November
